result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.clustering_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate local clustering coefficient for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L10560-L10656){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.clustering_coefficient(attr_name=None, return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The clustering coefficient measures the degree to which a node's neighbors are connected to each other. For a node `v`: `C(v) = (number of edges between neighbors) / (number of possible edges between neighbors) = (2 × triangles through v) / (degree(v) × (degree(v) - 1))` Returns `0.0` for nodes with degree < `2` (cannot form triangles). Range: `[0, 1]` where: - `0` = neighbors are not connected at all - `1` = neighbors form a complete graph (clique) ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store clustering coefficient values. If `None`, uses `clustering_coefficient` as the attribute name. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary mapping node IDs to clustering coefficients. If `False`, stores values as node attributes and returns the Graph for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float] or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to clustering coefficients (`0.0` to `1.0`). If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} High clustering coefficients indicate nodes in tightly-knit groups. The clustering coefficient is a key measure of network transitivity and is used to identify small-world networks. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calculate and store clustering coefficients: ::: {#05a7a49d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") .clustering_coefficient() # Stores as 'clustering_coefficient' attribute ) # All nodes have clustering coefficient 1.0 (complete triangle) ``` ::: Calculate clustering in a star graph: ::: {#ee75ec6d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="center") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("center", "A") .add_edge("center", "B") .add_edge("center", "C") ) clustering = graph.clustering_coefficient(return_dict=True) center_id = graph.get_id_from_label("center") # Returns 0.0 (no edges between spokes) clustering[center_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.0 ``` ::: :::
